Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
26 pages, 14 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers for the same number of loops during prefill and decode. Yet generation is strongly asymmetric: prefill reads the prompt once in parallel and takes under 3% of the wall time, while decoding runs token by token and takes over 97%. In this work, we ask whether prefill and decode should loop equally, and find that they should not. Untying the two loop counts lets a model read the prompt with more loops and decode each answer token with fewer. To make this work after pretraining, we introduce LoopBridge, a small adapter (2.4% of the parameters) with RoPE-commuting key-value maps that supports any trained prefill/decode pair and folds into the prompt cache once at prefill. With one decode loop on Ouro-2.6B, LoopBridge with four prefill loops raises the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 to 58.2, well above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5). On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking GSM8K, LoopBridge with four prefill and two decode loops matches the four-loop model's accuracy at 2.0x end-to-end throughput. Most of the gain arrives within two to five prefill loops, and the same pattern carries over to Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models, and looped decision models. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
